True)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Python%20setup%0A%0A%20%20%20%20NumPy%2C%20SciPy%2C%20pandas%2C%20and%20Matplotlib%20provide%20fitting%2C%20tables%2C%20and%20plots%3B%20IPython%20renders%20equations.%20Examples%20use%20simulated%20or%20explicitly%20constructed%20data%2C%20so%20no%20private%20experimental%20files%20are%20required.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20Curve%20fitting%20is%20the%20process%20of%20fitting%20a%20model%2C%20expressed%20in%20terms%20of%20a%20mathematical%20function%2C%20that%20depends%20on%20adjustable%20parameters%20to%20a%20series%20of%20data%20points%20and%20once%20adjusted%2C%20that%20curve%20has%20the%20best%20fit%20to%20the%20data%20points.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20model%20can%20be%20an%20arbitrary%20class%20of%20functions%20such%20as%20polynomials%20and%20the%20fit%20would%20determine%20the%20polynomial%20coefficients%20to%20simplily%20summarize%20the%20data%20or%20the%20model%20parameters%20can%20represent%20a%20underlying%20theory%20that%20the%20data%20are%20supposed%20to%20satisfy%20such%20as%20fitting%20an%20exponential%20function%20to%20data%20of%20a%20decay%20process%20to%20determine%20its%20decay%20rate%20or%20a%20parabola%20to%20the%20position%20data%20of%20an%20object%20falling%20to%20determine%20the%20gravity%20acceleration.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20general%20approach%20to%20the%20fitting%20procedure%20involves%20the%20definition%20of%20a%20merit%20function%20that%20measures%20the%20agreement%20between%20data%20and%20model.%20The%20model%20parameters%20are%20then%20adjusted%20to%20yield%20the%20best-fit%20parameters%20as%20a%20problem%20of%20minimization.%20A%20fitting%20procedure%20should%20provide%20(i)%20parameters%2C%20(ii)%20error%20estimates%20on%20the%20parameters%2C%20and%20(iii)%20a%20statistical%20measure%20of%20goodness-of-fit.%20When%20the%20third%20item%20suggests%20that%20the%20model%20is%20an%20unlikely%20match%20to%20the%20data%2C%20then%20items%20(i)%20and%20(ii)%20are%20probably%20worthless.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20(Numerical%20Recipes%202007%2C%20Bevington%20and%20Robinson%202002)%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Least%20squares%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Consider%20%24n%24%20data%20points%20%24(x_i%2C%20y_i)%2C%5C%3A%20i%3D1%2C%20%5Cdots%20%2C%20n%24%2C%20where%20%24x_i%24%20is%20the%20independent%20variable%20(or%20predictor)%20and%20%24y_i%24%20is%20the%20dependent%20variable%20(or%20response)%20to%20be%20fitted%20by%20a%20model%20function%20%24y%24%20with%20%24m%24%20adjustable%20parameters%20%24%5Cbeta_i%2C%5C%3A%20i%3D1%2C%20%5Cdots%20%2C%20m%24.%20The%20problem%20is%20to%20find%20the%20parameter%20values%20for%20the%20model%20which%20best%20fits%20the%20data.%20A%20classical%20solution%20is%20to%20find%20the%20best%20fit%20by%20minimizing%20the%20sum%20of%20the%20squared%20differences%20between%20data%20points%20and%20the%20model%20function%20(the%20sum%20of%20squared%20residuals%20as%20the%20merit%20function)%2C%20which%20is%20known%20as%20the%20least-squares%20fit%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Csum_%7Bi%3D1%7D%5E%7Bn%7D%20%5Cleft%5B%20y_i%20-%20y(x%20%7C%20%5Cbeta_1%20%5Cdots%20%5Cbeta_%7Bm%7D)%20%5Cright%5D%5E2%20%5C%3B%5C%3B%5C%3B%5C%3B%5C%3B%5C%3B%20%5Cmathrm%7Bminimize%5C%3B%20over%3A%7D%20%5C%3B%5C%3B%5C%3B%20%5Cbeta_1%20%5Cdots%20%5Cbeta_%7Bm%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Chi-Square**%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20If%20we%20consider%20that%20each%20response%20%24y_i%24%20has%20a%20measurement%20error%20or%20uncertainty%20described%20by%20a%20standard%20deviation%2C%20%24%5Csigma_i%24%2C%20the%20problem%20now%20is%20to%20minimize%20the%20following%20function%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Csum_%7Bi%3D1%7D%5E%7Bn%7D%20%5Cleft%5B%20%5Cfrac%7B%20y_i%20-%20y(x%20%7C%20%5Cbeta_1%20%5Cdots%20%5Cbeta_%7Bm%7D)%20%7D%7B%5Csigma_i%7D%20%5Cright%5D%5E2%20%3D%20%5Cchi%5E2%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Considering%20that%20the%20residuals%20are%20normally%20distributed%2C%20the%20sum%20of%20squared%20residuals%20divided%20by%20their%20variance%2C%20%24%5Csigma_i%5E2%24%2C%20by%20definition%20will%20have%20a%20%5Bchi-squared%20distribution%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FChi-squared_distribution)%2C%20%24%5Cchi%5E2%24.%20Once%20the%20best-fit%20parameters%20are%20found%2C%20the%20terms%20in%20the%20sum%20above%20are%20not%20all%20statistically%20independent%20and%20the%20probability%20distribution%20of%20%24%5Cchi%5E2%24%20will%20be%20the%20chi-squared%20distribution%20for%20%24n-m%24%20degrees%20of%20freedom.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20uncertainty%20%24%5Csigma_i%24%20can%20be%20seen%20as%20the%20inverse%20of%20the%20weights%20in%20a%20weighted%20sum%20(because%20less%20certainty%20we%20have%20about%20this%20measure).%20Larger%20%24%5Csigma_i%24%2C%20smaller%20the%20weight%20of%20%24y_i%24%20in%20the%20sum.%20If%20uncertainties%20are%20unknown%20and%20all%20observations%20receive%20equal%20weight%2C%20set%20all%20%24%5Csigma_i%3D1%24%20as%20a%20weighting%20convention.%20This%20does%20not%20mean%20the%20measurements%20have%20no%20uncertainty.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20A%20rough%20estimate%20of%20the%20goodness%20of%20fit%20is%20the%20reduced%20chi-square%20statistic%2C%20%24%5Cchi%5E2_%7Bred%7D%24%3A%20the%20%24%5Cchi%5E2%24%20value%20divided%20by%20the%20number%20of%20degrees%20of%20freedom%20(%24n-m%24).%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20For%20a%20correct%20model%20with%20independent%20normal%20errors%20and%20correctly%20specified%20standard%20deviations%2C%20reduced%20chi-square%20is%20expected%20near%20one%2C%20with%20sampling%20variability.%20A%20large%20value%20can%20reflect%20model%20error%20or%20underestimated%20uncertainties%3B%20a%20small%20value%20can%20reflect%20overestimated%20uncertainties.%20Rescaling%20errors%20to%20force%20a%20value%20of%20one%20is%20not%20model%20validation.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20**Exercise%201.**%20Two%20residuals%20are%20both%202%20units%2C%20but%20their%20stated%20SDs%20are%201%20and%202%20units.%20What%20are%20their%20contributions%20to%20chi-square%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%20details%20%7C%20Solution%20to%20Exercise%201%0A%20%20%20%20They%20contribute%20%24(2%2F1)%5E2%3D4%24%20and%20%24(2%2F2)%5E2%3D1%24.%20The%20less%20precise%20observation%20receives%20less%20influence.%20In%20the%20squared-residual%20objective%20the%20weights%20are%20inverse%20variances.%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Linear%20fit%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Let's%20derive%20the%20analytical%20expression%20for%20the%20least-square%20fit%20when%20the%20model%20function%20is%20a%20straight%20line%20(a.k.a.%20linear%20regression)%20and%20the%20dependent%20variable%20%24y_i%24%20has%20uncertainty%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20y(x)%20%3D%20y(x%20%7C%20a%2Cb)%20%3D%20a%20%2B%20bx%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20We%20want%20to%20find%20%24a%2C%20b%24%20such%20that%20minimizes%20the%20%24%5Cchi%5E2%24%20function%20defined%20above%20(a.k.a.%20%24%5Cchi%5E2%24%20fitting)%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cchi%5E2(a%2Cb)%20%3D%20%5Csum_%7Bi%3D1%7D%5E%7Bn%7D%20%5Cleft%5B%20%5Cfrac%7B%20y_i%20-%20(a%20%2B%20bx_i)%20%7D%7B%5Csigma_i%7D%20%5Cright%5D%5E2%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Using%20the%20property%20that%20at%20the%20minimum%20of%20%24%5Cchi%5E2%24%20its%20derivative%20is%20zero%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cfrac%7B%5Cpartial%20%5Cchi%5E2%7D%7B%5Cpartial%20a%7D%20%3D%20-2%20%5Csum_%7Bi%3D1%7D%5E%7Bn%7D%20%5Cfrac%7B%20y_i%20-%20a%20-%20bx_i%20%7D%7B%5Csigma_i%5E2%7D%20%3D%200%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A% etails%20%7C%20Solution%20to%20Exercise%204%0A%20%20%20%20The%20residual%20curvature%20suggests%20a%20missing%20nonlinear%20term%20or%20a%20wrong%20physical%20model.%20A%20high%20%24R%5E2%24%20can%20coexist%20with%20that%20pattern.%20Inspect%20the%20measurement%20process%20and%20compare%20a%20scientifically%20justified%20curved%20model.%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Confidence%20and%20prediction%20intervals%20for%20the%20linear%20fit%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Analog%20to%20the%20case%20for%20a%20random%20variable%20(see%20%5BConfidence%20and%20prediction%20intervals%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fconfidence_prediction_intervals.py))%2C%20we%20can%20estimate%20confidence%20and%20prediction%20intervals%20for%20the%20linear%20fit%20(for%20the%20deduction%20of%20these%20intervals%20see%20for%20example%20Montgomery%20(2013)).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Confidence%20interval**%0A%0A%20%20%20%20A%2095%25%20confidence%20interval%20for%20the%20linear%20fit%20gives%20the%2095%25%20probability%20that%20this%20interval%20around%20the%20linear%20fit%2C%20%24%5Chat%7B%5Cmu%7D_%7By%7Cx0%7D%24%2C%20contains%20the%20mean%20response%20of%20new%20values%2C%20%24%5Cmu_%7By%7Cx0%7D%24%2C%20at%20a%20specified%20value%2C%20%24x_0%24%2C%20and%20it%20is%20given%20by%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cleft%7C%20%5C%3A%20%5Chat%7B%5Cmu%7D_%7By%7Cx0%7D%20-%20%5Cmu_%7By%7Cx0%7D%20%5C%3A%20%5Cright%7C%20%5C%3B%20%5Cleq%20%5C%3B%20T_%7Bn-2%7D%5E%7B.975%7D%20%5C%3B%20%5Chat%7B%5Csigma%7D%20%5C%3B%20%5Csqrt%7B%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%7D%2B%5Cfrac%7B(x_0-%5Cbar%7Bx%7D)%5E2%7D%7B%5Csum_%7Bi%3D1%7D%5En%7B(x_i-%5Cbar%7Bx%7D)%5E2%7D%7D%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Where%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%5Chat%7B%5Cmu%7D_%7By%7Cx0%7D%20%3D%20a%20%2B%20bx_0%24%20is%20computed%20from%20the%20lineat%20fit.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24T_%7Bn-2%7D%5E%7B.975%7D%24%20is%20the%20%2497.5%5E%7Bth%7D%24%20percentile%20of%20the%20Student's%20t-distribution%20with%20n%E2%88%922%20degrees%20of%20freedom.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%5Chat%7B%5Csigma%7D%24%20is%20the%20standard%20deviation%20of%20the%20error%20term%20in%20the%20linear%20fit%20(residuals)%20given%20by%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Chat%7B%5Csigma%7D%20%3D%20%5Csqrt%7B%5Csum_%7Bi%3D1%7D%5En%7B%5Cfrac%7B(y_i-%5Chat%7By%7D)%5E2%7D%7Bn-2%7D%7D%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Prediction%20interval**%0A%0A%20%20%20%20A%2095%25%20prediction%20interval%20for%20the%20linear%20fit%20gives%20the%2095%25%20probability%20that%20this%20interval%20around%20the%20linear%20fit%2C%20%24%5Chat%7By%7D_0%24%2C%20contains%20a%20new%20observation%2C%20%24y_0%24%2C%20at%20a%20specified%20value%2C%20%24x_0%24%2C%20and%20it%20is%20given%20by%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cleft%7C%20%5C%3A%20%5Chat%7By%7D_0%20-%20y_0%20%5C%3A%20%5Cright%7C%20%5C%3B%20%5Cleq%20%5C%3B%20T_%7Bn-2%7D%5E%7B.975%7D%20%5C%3B%20%5Chat%7B%5Csigma%7D%20%5C%3B%20%5Csqrt%7B1%20%2B%20%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%7D%2B%5Cfrac%7B(x_0-%5Cbar%7Bx%7D)%5E2%7D%7B%5Csum_%7Bi%3D1%7D%5En%7B(x_i-%5Cbar%7Bx%7D)%5E2%7D%7D%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Where%20%24%5Chat%7By%7D_0%20%3D%20a%20%2B%20bx_0%24%20is%20computed%20from%20the%20lineat%20fit.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Implementation%20in%20Python**%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Here%20is%20an%20implementation%20of%20the%20linear%20fit%20with%20the%20confidence%20and%20prediction%20intervals%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(np%2C%20plt%2C%20stats)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20def%20linearfit_1(x%2C%20y%2C%20yerr)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22%22%22Linear%20fit%20of%20x%20and%20y%20with%20uncertainty%20and%20plots%20results.%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20(x%2C%20y)%20%3D%20(np.asarray(x)%2C%20np.asarray(y))%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20n%20%3D%20y.size%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20(p%2C%20_cov)%20%3D%20
